app.notes: Static Vite build of the repo (React 19 + Vite 8, Node 22.23.5 pinned in mise.toml). Rebuild with `npm ci && npx vite build --config .ui-capture/vite.capture.config.js` from the repo root; that config extends the repo's vite.config.js and only swaps integrations for stubs (no repo source files changed). Output is .ui-capture/out (index.html entry, SPA fallback ok). DATA: the app stores everything in browser localStorage. The capture build boots via .ui-capture/seed/boot.js, which on first load writes a seeded trip document (generator: .ui-capture/seed/seedData.js) into the app's own key 'trip-command-center/v4-public' before React mounts, and sets the viewer profile to the Jiangs (marker key 'ui-capture/seed-version'; clear localStorage to reseed). Seed = the app's built-in Pine Mountain Lake / Yosemite weekend (Apr 9-12, 3 families: Parkers LA, Jiangs SF, Riveras Reno) extended to look like ~3 months of group planning: ~65 checklist tasks across families/days (mostly done, some open, short and long notes, created/edited stamps Jan-Apr 2026), 15 meals incl. road stops and pending treats, 10 activities (Go/Watch/Pending, incl. parked ideas), edited expense ledger (real-looking amounts, manual split, settled/open), family responsibilities, stay notes, and page notes with edit attribution. The app re-derives families/locations/itinerary/stay/expenses from its built-in seed on every load (refreshSeededDoc), so those collections can't grow beyond the built-in records; only their edited fields persist. On load the app snaps the timeline cursor to the real clock relative to April 9-12 of the current year, so in November the cursor sits at trip end ('No live items in this window'); scrub the bottom timeline to see live state. MAIN AREAS: top command bar with 'Working as' family switcher; left rail (current situation, daily briefing, travel units); center live map (offline stub basemap with family routes, vehicles, facilities, layer/family/day focus, NOAA weather intel); bottom mission timeline with playback; right inspector rail (briefing, checklist, notes). Icon nav on the far left: Itinerary, Stay, Meals, Activities, Expenses, Families. Verified with a jsdom smoke test (.ui-capture/smoke.mjs). Headless Chromium couldn't launch inside the build sandbox, so I never inspected it visually.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):

Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.

List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. # Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). - static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4455/ (it gets PORT=4455). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
